sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year, from $22.7 billion in FY2016 to $31.7 billion in FY2025 [F198][F1][F9].
Operating income compounded faster than revenue, at 5.8% against 3.8% a year, lifting operating margin from 22.9% in FY2016 to 27.2% in FY2025 [F199][F198][F20][F28].

Operating income fell 19.9% in FY2020 [D156]; the filing ties this to CCR settlement impairments and COVID-19 volume losses [P60], with impairments rising to $984 million from a credit of $8.0 million in FY2019 [X103][X102].
Revenue rose 17.1% in FY2022 to $28.7 billion [D239][F6], which the filing links to higher rate-case revenues, favorable weather and volumes [P26].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue [D541] and added 3.6pp of the 5.6% revenue growth [D543][D358].
Residential electricity sales grew 6.6% and added 2.8pp [D775][D776]; the pack holds no passage explaining that FY2025 move.
Operating expenses rose 5.3% against 5.6% revenue growth [D372][D358], lifting operating income 8.8% [D359] and giving a 41.4% incremental margin [D378].
Diluted EPS compounded at 8.2% against 9.7% for net income, because diluted shares rose from 691 million to 777 million [F202][F200][X106][X115].
Operating margin of 27.2% [F28][D932] is the window high, against a 22.9% median [D933] and a 19.7% low in FY2020 [D931].
In FY2025 that ranks at the 75th percentile of four utilities peers, whose median is 25.7% [D949][D950].
The largest operating-margin move, a 3.8pp fall in FY2020 [D168], traced to a $519 million rise in impairment charges tied to the CCR settlement [P53].
The effective tax rate was 11.2% in FY2025 against 31.0% in FY2016 [D345][D7], and the filings cited do not explain the decline.
Interest expense reached $3.63 billion in FY2025 [X63], keeping net margin of 15.7% [F47] well below operating margin of 27.2% [F28].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion [F77][D346] was 2.48x net income, inside the 2.12x to 3.48x range of all years except FY2020 (6.43x) [D184][D268][D142].
Free cash flow was negative $1.69 billion in FY2025 [F97], or -0.34x net income [D347], after a $48.0 million surplus in FY2024 [F96].
Capex absorbed 44.2% of revenue [D342] and ran at 1.82x D&A [D348], so plant spending outpaces depreciation by a wide margin.
Operating cash flow fell 28.5% in FY2022 to $5.93 billion [D244][F74], as under-collected fuel costs were deferred and financed with borrowings [P36].
Net cash was -$89.6 billion in FY2025 [D352], or -282.3% of revenue [D353], ranking at the 25th percentile of four peers against a -228.4% median [D953][D954].
Return on average equity of 9.7% [D357] ranks lowest of the four peers, against a 12.6% median [D955][D956].
Total debt rose from $50.4 billion in FY2016 [D13] to $89.8 billion in FY2025 [D351], with $11.9 billion of debt issued that year [X133].
Borrowing rather than free cash flow has funded the build-out, so rising total debt [D351] is the main balance-sheet risk.
Current liabilities rose 8.7% to $21.0 billion in FY2025 [D369][F157], leaving the current ratio at 0.55x [F177], close to its 0.53x window low [D943].
The 0.1-year cash cover of burn [R2][D356] is a benign flag, since deficits are debt-funded, with $11.9 billion issued in FY2025 [X133].
Net cash has been negative for nine straight years [R3], reaching -$89.6 billion in FY2025 [D352] alongside capex of 44.2% of revenue [D342].
Free cash flow was below 80% of net income in FY2023 to FY2025, at -0.96x [D269], 0.01x [D309] and -0.34x [D347] [R4].
The FY2023 revenue decline [R5] is benign: revenue was flat at 0.0% [D280] on $28.7 billion [F7].
An operating margin below the 22.9% window median [D933], from 27.2% in FY2025 [F28], would reverse the expansion; check the FY2026 10-K.
A free cash flow margin below the -5.8% window median [D939] would confirm the capex-led deficit; above the 0.2% window high [D938] would signal a turn, in the FY2026 10-K.
Net cash worse than -282.3% of revenue [D353] would widen the gap to the -228.4% peer median [D954]; check the FY2026 10-K.
